title: Pricing by hours per project for Timber floor restoration
audience: Owners and supervisors who write quotes for cleaning projects and need a price that covers cost and earns a margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour from the owner's own figures
Estimate project hours, including set-up, travel and checking time
Build a quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit
instruction.body: A floor restoration is a sequence of stages: protecting the room, sanding through grit steps, cleaning and dust control, filling, coating, and drying between coats. Each stage takes time that depends on the floor's condition and the room's shape, so hours show where the money goes. No source read for this course gives sanding or refinishing hours for timber floors. The one sourced rate is an area range, and an area range is not a time standard. The hours on each stage must come from your own time logs.

instruction.heading: Build the cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Take the total cost of running the business over a period and divide it by the productive hours in the same period. Include wages with on-costs such as leave and superannuation where your arrangements need them (business.gov.au, 1 October 2026), vehicle running costs, dust extraction, sanding discs, finishes, insurance, administration and premises. Productive hours are chargeable hours on site, not the paid hours on a roster. If you pay for 40 hours and 30 are chargeable, the cost per productive hour is higher than the hourly wage.

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours
instruction.body: Break each room into stages: protection and furniture moving, each sanding grit, edging, dust clean-down, filling, each coat, and drying. Estimate each stage at a standard speed, then add set-up, pack-down, travel and a checking allowance. Xero's guide suggests adding 10 to 20 percent to job estimates for unexpected work (Xero Australia, 3 September 2026). That is a range to test against your own records, not a figure sourced for timber floors. Record the actual hours for each room and the reason for any difference, and correct the next estimate.

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price
instruction.body: Multiply the crew hours by the cost per productive hour to get the cost of the job. Add a margin that reflects your target and the risk in the job, such as a floor with deep damage or painted edges that need extra work. Apply your materials policy and your minimum charge. Then check the result against the sourced area range, which is a sense check and not a rate. The Oneflare guide gives a general refinish range of $25 to $50 per square metre (Oneflare, no date shown). A price that falls well outside that range needs a reason you can state.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest
instruction.body: A quote states the scope, the hours or price basis, the exclusions, what the client must provide, and how long the quote is valid. Exclusions for timber work usually include board replacement, gap filling beyond the stated amount, and any lead or hazardous-material testing or removal, which are priced separately if the client asks. Do not show the internal cost per hour to the client unless your policy says to. Re-quote when the scope changes.

instruction.heading: Review your estimates
instruction.body: Compare estimated and actual hours for at least the first ten rooms of each type. If the variance is consistently above your agreed threshold, change the standard time, the margin or the scope rules. A pricing method is finished only when actual hours match quoted hours closely enough for the work to make money.

procedure: Gather the year's total business costs and the chargeable hours achieved in the same period.
Divide total costs by chargeable hours to get the cost per productive hour.
Break each room into sanding, coating and drying stages, and estimate each stage time as a range.
Add set-up, pack-down, travel and checking time as named lines.
Multiply total crew hours by the cost per productive hour, then apply the margin for risk and target.
Apply the materials policy, the exclusions for board and lead-related work, and the minimum charge.
Write the quote with scope, hours basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
Record actual hours after each job and compare them with the estimate.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only, not market rates. A 20 square metre hardwood room is a full refinish. The owner estimates 11.5 crew-hours in total: protection and furniture moving 1.0, sanding 4.0, edging 1.5, dust clean-down 1.0, two coats 2.0, set-up and checking 1.0, and travel 1.0. The cost per productive hour is $60 AUD (illustrative). The target margin on price is 25 per cent (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the cost of the job, what is the price, and does the price sit inside the sourced area range?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cost is 11.5 crew-hours multiplied by $60 AUD, which is $690 AUD. A 25 per cent margin on price means the price is the cost divided by 0.75, which gives $920 AUD. The Oneflare general range is $25 to $50 per square metre, which for 20 square metres is $500 to $1,000 (Oneflare, no date shown). The illustrative price sits inside that range, so the owner has a reason to believe it is plausible. The range is only a sense check. If the hours were wrong, the price would be wrong too, so the owner still checks the stages against the room.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative: the same room has painted floor edges that need extra stripping by hand. The estimate rises by 2 crew-hours for the edges, and the quote's terms say that painted edges are priced as an extra if they are found on site.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the revised price, and what must be true before the extra is added to the bill?
workedExamples.reasoning: Two extra crew-hours at the illustrative $60 AUD cost $120 AUD. Divided by 0.75, the illustrative price rises by $160, to $1,080 AUD. The extra can be added only if the quote's terms allow it and the client agreed the change in writing before the extra work started. Any lead-related testing or safe-work method for painted edges is set out in the safety section and priced on its own line.

equipmentAndPpe: Quote worksheet or spreadsheet with room stages and hours
Time log for each room, with estimated and actual columns
Measuring tape or laser measure for area estimates
PPE as listed in {{business:safety.required_ppe}}, with respiratory protection and dust controls as set out in the safety section

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the hourly wage alone.
commonErrors.prevention: Include on-costs, dust extraction, abrasives, finishes, insurance and administration in the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Counting paid hours as productive hours.
commonErrors.prevention: Use chargeable hours only when calculating the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out dust clean-down and drying time from the estimate. Gap: no sourced timber sanding hour standard exists.
commonErrors.prevention: Add these as named lines on every estimate, and check the hours against your own logs.

commonErrors.error: Quoting with no exclusions for board replacement, gap filling or painted-edge work.
commonErrors.prevention: List what is excluded and priced separately, what the client provides, and the access assumptions.

commonErrors.error: Never comparing estimates with actual hours.
commonErrors.prevention: Record actual hours after each job and review the variance monthly.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This is pricing guidance only. The ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited under the Australian Consumer Law (ACCC, 15 July 2026). State or territory fair trading rules also apply and differ, so check the rules for your state.

Victoria only: WorkSafe Victoria guidance (reviewed 17 April 2026) says wood dust is carcinogenic to humans, that sanding needs local exhaust ventilation, and that a half-face P2 respirator would be sufficient in usual cases. Include the dust controls and the respirator cost in the quote as lines, and check the rule for your state.

NSW only: NSW LeadSmart says lead paint may be present in painted timber floor edges and skirting in homes built before 1970, and recommends a professional trained in lead paint work. Price any lead-related testing, removal or safe-work method on its own line, and check the rule for the state where you work.

Pay rates, allowances and on-costs for employees may be set by an award or enterprise agreement. Check which one applies to each worker before using any cost figure. This lesson does not state those rates.

qualityStandard: Each quote shows scope, hours or price basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the owner's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for at least the first ten rooms of each type and compared with the estimate.
No quote is issued without a margin decision and a minimum-charge check.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing scope, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Job time log with estimated and actual hours
summary: Hours make floor work visible, so start every quote from stage hours.
Cost per productive hour uses chargeable time, and includes dust extraction and finishes.
Gap: no sourced timber sanding hours exist. Use the Oneflare area range only as a sense check.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour for a floor refinish?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker
Wages with on-costs, dust extraction, abrasives, finishes, insurance and administration, divided by chargeable hours
The average area rate of competitors in the local area
The deposit and the late fee the client paid

knowledgeChecks.question: A room is estimated at 11.5 crew-hours and takes 15. What is the right response?
options: Record the actual hours, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate, since the client has already paid
Reduce the crew's paid hours on the next job
Raise the price for this client only and change nothing else

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a timber floor quote need an exclusions list?
options: To hide the margin from the client
To show what the price covers, so scope changes can be priced and disputes are reduced
To lower the client's expectations of the finish
